en: The Philippine Sea Plate subducts beneath Eurasia, melting rock into magma that feeds Mayon Volcano's frequent eruptions.
Warm Pacific Ocean waters evaporate and spin into typhoons that strike Eastern Visayas first.
Heavy monsoon rains wash soil into the Cagayan River, raising its water level and causing downstream floods.
Rising ocean temperatures cause coral bleaching in Tubbataha Reef by expelling the colorful algae living inside them.
Underground magma heats groundwater in Albay, creating steam that spins turbines at the Tiwi Geothermal Plant.
A massive ancient volcanic eruption collapsed the caldera floor, allowing rainwater to fill it and form Taal Lake.
Logging removes tree roots in the Sierra Madre, weakening the soil and causing deadly landslides during heavy rains.
Rainwater dissolves the limestone in Puerto Princesa, carving the massive underground chambers of the Subterranean River.
Mountain gravity pulls rainwater down through the Ifugao Rice Terraces, naturally irrigating the stepped paddies below.
Cold Siberian air masses push south during Amihan, bringing cool, dry weather to the entire Philippines.
Tectonic plates grind along the Valley Fault System, releasing built-up stress as sudden, shaking earthquakes in Metro Manila.
Lower ice-age sea levels exposed the ocean floor, creating a land bridge that connected Palawan to mainland Asia.
